## 2026-11-27, scheduled operator cycle: closed the 15-plus-times-recurring external-timeout fingerprint-stripping defect with a pre-push backstop, instead of re-confirming exhaustion a 48th time

**Did.** Attached per Step 0 (shallow detached checkout, real `fetch --unshallow`, 772 commits fast-forwarded, `checkout main`, `merge --ff-only` onto `origin/main`, tree clean). Read CLAUDE.md, BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md in full, OWNER-ACTIONS.md "Start here", GOALS.md, and the last entries of ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md before touching anything.

**Verified, not cited.** GitHub's 30 open issues re-pulled live via the API: unchanged, every one `decision` or `blocked-on-art`, none from Phil; `git log --author=phil` still stale, matching every cycle today. Production network to `6s-success.com` re-tested directly: still policy-blocked (403 from the agent proxy), not assumed. `inbox_agent.py --apply`: no mail credential here. `cold_read_ledger.py --next`: 316/316 ledgered, 0 candidates. `room_guide_underperformance.py --check-history` fresh: every partial row site-wide carries a prior-mention citation, nothing new. `ops/rotate_nightly_log.py --check`: clean, 14-day window.

**Found instead of re-confirming.** Ran `preflight.py --skip-tests` myself under a 170s external `timeout`, the exact anti-pattern `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md` already names at least 15 separate times since 2026-09: it killed the process mid-`gate_generator_ownership`, after that gate's own generator chain had rewritten ~166 live `site/` pages but before its own restore step ran, leaving every one of them with its `?v=` cache-bust hash stripped, uncommitted. Every one of those 15-plus prior occurrences was caught only by a human or agent happening to read `git status` before pushing; none of them produced a control that cannot be skipped by forgetting. `preflight.py`'s own early "fingerprints" gate (`ops/fingerprint_assets.py --check`) runs before `gate_generator_ownership` ever dirties the tree, so it had already reported clean earlier in the very same interrupted run and would not catch this on a second look without a fresh full pass.

**Fixed at the point that cannot be skipped.** Added a sixth check to `.githooks/pre-push`, same shape and length as the five already there (fast, pure file I/O, no browser or network, same `--no-verify` escape hatch): `python ops/fingerprint_assets.py --check`, which already existed and already runs in under 0.12s. Proved fail-then-pass directly against the real hook, not a simulation: stripped one `?v=` hash from `site/quest.html` by hand, ran `.githooks/pre-push` with no ref args, watched it print the STALE line and exit 1; restored the file, ran it again, exit 0. Discarded the self-inflicted 166-page drift itself with `git stash` (inspected first: every changed line was either a stripped/changed `?v=` hash or this run's own dashboard checkpoint, nothing else), confirmed `ops/fingerprint_assets.py --check` clean against HEAD before planting the test fault, then dropped the stash. Regenerated the command deck fresh on the clean tree.

**Went well.** Caught a real, long-recurring defect by reading `git status` after a routine step rather than trusting the dashboard regen to be side-effect free, then closed it structurally instead of discarding and moving on like every prior occurrence.

**Did not go well.** This is the 16th time this exact shape has been found; the standing advice ("do not external-timeout-kill preflight.py while gate_generator_ownership is running") never once stopped a cycle from doing it anyway, including this one, because the advice lives in prose nobody reads before choosing a command. The gate added here does not stop the mistake, only its consequence from reaching a push.

**Changing next cycle.** Nothing further on this; if it recurs a 17th time, the pre-push hook should now catch it before main is ever touched, which is the point.

**Next.** Same standing Phil-gated queue, `OWNER-ACTIONS.md` "Start here", cheapest first (#64 traffic read, #58 Stripe description, #46 YouTube OAuth). No push notification: last real push 2026-11-26T14:08:20Z, 48h floor not elapsed, and issue #42 already tells Phil the cadence is saturated; nothing here changes that fact for him.

Pushed to main: this log entry, `.githooks/pre-push`, regenerated command deck. Not customer-facing, `IndexNow` not applicable (no `site/` page content changed, only a dev-side git hook).

Widened the guard to also cover zones on the heading surface, proved the 76 existing test cases still pass, then ran a full before/after `score_rows()` diff across both corpora before shipping (CLAUDE.md 5d) and caught two real regressions the widening itself created: "how to organize baking supplies in kitchen" (and 2 "kitchen larder" siblings) dropped from a genuine, correct 1.0 on Pantry's own zone to a worse in-room partial, and "how to store outdoor furniture cushions in garage" lost Patio/Deck's actually-more-relevant answer to a weaker Garage one. Added a "zone already at 1.0 is left alone" carve-out; it fixed the kitchen/larder cases but not the garage one, because a genuinely-correct cross-room zone can score under 1.0 too. No score-based rule separates the two classes reliably. Reverted the whole change rather than ship a net-harmful fix.

Grepped the actual query against the log afterward: already found and declined twice before (A85-era and a later cold-read), for exactly this reason ("a zone's higher score is ordinarily the more trustworthy signal, the opposite of what makes the article-only override safe"). My own full-corpus diff is the concrete proof that prior decline lacked; nothing here was new, but the decline is now backed by evidence, not caution alone. Should have grepped before implementing, not after.

Checked before acting (CLAUDE.md 5d): that gate compares `EDITION_DATE` against `_last_commit_epoch("content/book")`, the whole directory, not the specific files `ops/build_epub.py` actually reads (`book_chapter_files()`'s 50 chapters, `assets/`, the front matter). A263's own fix touched `content/book/"6S Success Home Edition - Sample (Chapters 1-30).html"`, a separate, hand-authored file `ops/build_sample_html.py` reads for the free web sample, never read by the EPUB builder at all. **Verified:** `python ops/tests/test_last_commit_epoch_shallow_boundary.py` and `python ops/tests/test_gate_store_art.py` (the two existing callers of `_last_commit_epoch`) both still pass unchanged. New `ops/tests/test_gate_epub_edition_date_scoped.py` (3 cases): a bogus extra pathspec does not change the result, the real gate is clean against the real repo today, and `book_chapter_files()` genuinely excludes the unrelated sample file. Fail-then-pass proved directly against the real repository's own git history, not a synthetic fixture: the old unscoped call reads 2026-11-26 and would FAIL against `EDITION_DATE=2026-10-02`; the new scoped call does not.

**quest.html's `role="listitem"` on a `<button>`:** invalid per HTML-AAM (a native `<button>` cannot carry a non-widget role), axe's `aria-allowed-role`. Fixed in `site/assets/js/quest.js`'s `renderSymptomList()` (hand-written, not generator-owned): each symptom button is now wrapped in its own `<div role="listitem">`, with the `role` removed from the `<button>` itself, preserving `#sym-list`'s own `role="list"` semantics. `#sym-list .btn{width:100%}` is a descendant selector, unaffected by the extra wrapper level; the flex column's default `align-items:stretch` keeps the new wrapper full width, confirmed visually unchanged.

**The "3 print-pack downloads" turned out to be a much bigger and differently-shaped defect than the note suggested, once actually scanned (not a sample):** `all_pages()`, the function every other axe-aware gate reads from, deliberately excludes `site/downloads/`, so A262's own full-site scan never actually covered it, and its brief mention of "the book-sample download" undersold what was there. The free sample book (`site/downloads/"6S Success Home Edition - Sample (Chapters 1-30).html"`, this site's primary lead magnet) renders 137 inline callout boxes (6S Tip, Common Mistake, Quick Win, Family Challenge) as bare `<aside class="callout ...">`, each an unnamed `complementary` landmark nested inside its own chapter `<section>`, `landmark-complementary-is-top-level`, confirmed on all 137 nodes by a full scan, not a sample. These are inline pull-quotes within running chapter text, not page-level sidebars, so the correct fix is `role="note"` (ARIA's own definition: "content that is parenthetic or ancillary to the main content"), not a restructure. Patched the true source, `content/book/"6S Success Home Edition - Sample (Chapters 1-30).html"` (hand-authored, no other generator writes it), with a scoped regex adding `role="note"` to all 137 tags, then regenerated through the real chain, `ops/build_sample_html.py --apply` (which also reruns `fingerprint_assets.py`, correctly bumping `quest.js`'s cache-bust hash on every page that references it, including `site/sw.js`'s own precache list and `site/quest.html`).

Separately, the three standalone printable downloads (`6S-Micro-Zone-Map.html`, `6S-Standards-Pack.html`, `6S-Zone-Scoring-and-Audit-Template.html`) each open `<body>` directly onto `<div class="intro">...</div>` before their own `<main>`, so that intro text sits outside every ARIA landmark on the page, axe's `region` rule (all page content must be contained by a landmark), confirmed on all three by the same scan. Each generator's own comment explains this was deliberate, so a screen reader could skip the intro to reach the sheets or the reverse; the fix keeps that separation but wraps the intro in `<header>` instead of leaving it landmark-less (a `<header>` not itself nested in article/aside/main/nav/section carries the `banner` landmark). Fixed at the generator level (CLAUDE.md 5b): `ops/build_zone_map_pack.py`, `ops/build_standards.py`, `ops/build_corporate_asset.py`, each wraps its existing intro markup in `<header>...</header>`; none has a parent-sensitive CSS selector on `.intro`, confirmed by grep before editing. Regenerated all three; `build_standards.py` only writes `build/`, so its own documented copy step (`cp build/6S-Standards-Pack.html site/downloads/`) was run too, matching what `gate_standards_pack_current` already checks for.

## Same cycle, minutes later: a real CI gap found and gated, correcting this entry's own "no new preflight gate" line below

While pushing the entry below, `preflight.py`'s own `gate_checks_yml_real_gap` briefly, correctly flagged this cycle's own not-yet-pushed commits as unverified work (expected: the push had not happened yet). Tracing why rather than dismissing it as noise found a real, standing gap: `ops/cycle-signal.json` and `ops/last-owner-notification.json`, two pure-bookkeeping files under `ops/**` written every cycle the same way `ops/state.json`/`ops/dashboard.html`/`ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md` already are, were never added to `checks.yml`'s push-path exclusions alongside those four, so a commit touching only one of them was still starting a full Checks run and, under the workflow's own cancel-in-progress group, could cancel a real fix's in-flight verification, the exact 2026-09-13 outage shape `gate_checks_excludes_generated_files` already exists to prevent, just for two files it had never been told about.

Fixed in `checks.yml` (both `push` and `pull_request` blocks), and per CLAUDE.md 10b, hardened the two gates that should have caught this rather than just the symptom: extended `gate_checks_excludes_generated_files`'s required list and `CI_PATH_COVERAGE_EXEMPT` (read by `gate_ci_path_filter_covers_preflight_inputs`) to require both new paths, and extended `test_gate_checks_excludes_generated_files.py` with a fail-then-pass case for the two new paths going missing again. Proved it can fail: ran the test suite against the unmodified `checks.yml` first and watched both gates correctly FAIL by name (`ci-path-coverage` naming `ops/cycle-signal.json`, caught independently before the test was even touched), then confirmed clean after the fix, 6/6 and 13/13 on each test file. `preflight.py --skip-tests` re-run live after committing: 0 FAIL.

This corrects the entry below's own "no new preflight gate (10b): no new defect class found" line, written before this was found a few minutes later in the same cycle.

## Scheduled operator cycle, 2026-11-18 (~04:1x slot): closed the last named shallow-clone instance (gate_status_currency's commit-range miscount), then found a duplicate commit of my own mid-cycle and dropped it rather than ship it

**Did.** Attached clean: `fetch`, genuine `fetch --unshallow`, `checkout main`, `merge --ff-only`, no reset or force. Read `BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md` in full, `ROADMAP-2026-2029.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the last four `ops/NIGHTLY-LOG.md` entries before picking anything. `preflight.py --skip-tests` run live first: 0 FAIL, 31 warnings, all standing. 31 open GitHub issues re-pulled live: unchanged, all `decision`/`blocked-on-art`, none from Phil since #65 (confirmed directly via the API, not cited). `inbox_agent.py --apply`: no mail credential, standing gap.

**First attempt was a duplicate, caught before it shipped twice.** Picked up the 03:0x PM check-in's own handoff (harden `build_seo.py`'s `_committed_date()` and `check_cron_cadence.py`'s `last_changed()` against the shallow-boundary false-positive already fixed in `cold_read_ledger.py`) and fixed both independently. On push, found a concurrent 03:4x PM check-in had landed the identical fix minutes earlier (`3394d1a5b`). Compared both diffs directly rather than assume: same two functions, same guard, same shape. Rebased onto `origin/main` and used `git rebase --skip` on my own now-redundant commit instead of force-pushing over or duplicating the fix; verified the tree afterward carried their fix and none of mine, so nothing shipped twice.

**The real find this cycle.** That same PM check-in named a differently-shaped remaining risk: `gate_status_currency()` in `ops/preflight.py` resolves STATUS.md's last-edit commit via `git log -1 -- STATUS.md` with no boundary guard, then diffs that hash against HEAD to count material commits STATUS.md never mentioned. On a shallow clone, a boundary commit with no visible parent gets credited with touching every path in its own tree, so if STATUS.md was not really edited since before the boundary, "last" silently resolves to the boundary's own hash. Unlike the date-only instances, this miscounts a commit *range*: on a deep shallow clone it can overcount unrelated history as unmentioned material commits and warn falsely; on an exactly-HEAD boundary (the common depth-1 shape) it silently reports zero unmentioned commits, a false "current" verdict with nothing actually measured, the CLAUDE.md 0.4 shape ("unknown is not unused") rather than the "wrong date" shape the other four fixes caught.

**Verified, not assumed.** Confirmed the guard would have caught nothing by coincidence: a monkeypatch test using the *real* last-touch hash as the faked boundary produced no behavioural difference between old and new code (the real range from that point is only 2 unmentioned material commits, below threshold), so a naive fail-then-pass against real history would have proven nothing. Rebuilt the test with fully synthetic git plumbing (boundary resolution, a 9-commit unmentioned range, each commit touching a material path) and proved it fails against the unguarded gate (a real false warning fires) and passes once the guard lands. Re-grepped every remaining raw `git log -1 -- path` caller across `ops/*.py`: all are now either guarded (`cold_read_ledger.py`, `build_seo.py`, `check_cron_cadence.py`, `preflight.py`'s own `_last_commit_epoch`/`gate_status_currency`), refuse to run while shallow (`affiliate_report.py`), or are path-independent (`dashboard.py`'s bare `git log -1 --format=%s`, HEAD's own commit, immune by construction). `check_urls.py` (236/236), `audit_pages.py` (0 findings), `cold_read_ledger.py --stale` (0) all clean. `preflight.py --skip-tests` re-run live to full completion after commit: 0 FAIL, 32 warnings, all standing.

**Went well:** catching my own duplicate before pushing it, by comparing diffs rather than assuming a title match meant identical scope, and resolving it with `rebase --skip` rather than a destructive reset. Also: this cycle's own synthetic-plumbing test is a better fail-then-pass proof than the sibling fixes' real-hash monkeypatches, which (as shown above) can pass against unfixed code by coincidence when the real repository state does not happen to exercise the bug.

**Did not go well:** running the same handoff a concurrent session was already mid-flight on cost a full attempt's worth of work before the duplication was caught; neither cycle had a way to see the other was active.

**Changing next cycle:** none beyond what's already standing.

**Next:** no further named instance of this defect class remains; all raw `git log -1 -- path` callers are accounted for. 31 open `decision`/`blocked-on-art` GitHub issues, none from Phil since #65; issue #42's cadence question still open since 2026-11-14.

Checked Step 2 directly: the prior cycle's handoff ("confirm run 817's re-trigger actually succeeds") was genuinely finished, re-verified against the Actions API, not cited: `publish-image.yml` run 818 (commit `59867f5f9`) completed `success` at 20:41:39Z.

While checking production freshness I watched `deploy.yml` run 427 fire live (triggered off that same success, for `main`'s tip by then, `a09eb7464`) and FAIL at 20:43:48Z, a real, current, customer-facing-adjacent signal, not a stale one: `VERDICT production is serving a DIFFERENT build ... image build for this commit: unknown ... could not ask GitHub what the image build is doing (no gh, no auth, or no network), so why production differs is UNCHECKED.` Pulled the job log directly rather than trusting the gate's summary. Root cause: `ops/deploy.py`'s `classify_publish()`/`_gh_runs()` shells out to `gh run list` to tell a benign registry-pull lag apart from a real stuck/failed image build, but `deploy.yml`'s job `permissions:` block granted only `contents: write` (no `actions: read`) and its `Deploy` step never exported `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so `gh` always had no auth and the classifier always fell into the uninformative `unknown` branch, on every mismatch, since this workflow was written. `checks.yml` already carries the exact working pattern for this repo's own `gh` usage (`permissions: actions: read` plus `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` on the step that calls it); mirrored both onto `deploy.yml`.

This does not make the current mismatch disappear (build-id lag between the image GHCR has and the commit `main` is now at is real, and `classify_publish` is correctly designed to still fail the job rather than guess), but it fixes the diagnosis so the next run says `building`/`ready`/`failed`/`none` with real advice instead of `unknown`, closing a gap that has silently made every past deploy-mismatch unresolvable from the log alone. `ops/tests/test_deploy_publish_state.py` (16/16, logic untouched, confirms this was pure wiring) and a YAML parse check both run directly. ## 2026-11-14, scheduled operator cycle: a self-inflicted stray fixture caused a real preflight FAIL, root caused and fixed rather than just cleaned up

**Did.** Attached clean: fetch, fetch --unshallow, checkout main, ff-only onto origin/main. Read CLAUDE.md, BACKLOG-2026-09-07.md (sections 0-7), the last several NIGHTLY-LOG.md entries. GitHub's 31 open issues re-pulled live via the API: unchanged since 2026-11-08, all decision/P0/blocked-on-art, none from Phil. inbox_agent.py --apply: no mail credential in this sandbox. All six rotators' own --check: CLEAN. preflight.py --skip-tests: every gate passed, 32 warnings, all standing. Mined the room-guide tier directly rather than cite "exhausted": confirmed live, every room between 4% and 14% uncovered on partial rows alone, 0 genuine gap rows anywhere, matching gate_room_guide_mining_diminishing_returns's own standing warning.

**Ran the full python ops/preflight.py (with gate_tests, not skipped) live in the background rather than defer it again, and it found a real FAIL.** test_audit_catalog.py: "the correct price $19 of 'The Whole House Print Pack' was reported as drift." Checked before believing it (CLAUDE.md 5d): the real catalogue audit was clean, 0 findings, so nothing was ever actually wrong with a live price. Root caused rather than re-run until green: an earlier background preflight run this same cycle had been killed by my own mistaken `timeout 110 ... &` wrapper mid-gate_tests, and test_audit_catalog.py's own "a wrong price must be caught" case had left site/_audit_catalog_fixture_<pid>.html behind stating a deliberately wrong $29 price for this exact SKU, because a SIGTERM skips that test's own finally-block cleanup. preflight.py's gate_no_stray_probe_files sweep, which would otherwise delete a dead-pid leftover like this one, runs before gate_tests in main()'s own ordering, so it cannot clean up a mess gate_tests makes later in the same pass. Reproduced standalone with no concurrent process running at all, ruling out a live-collision race before touching anything.

**Fixed at the root, not just the symptom.** audit_catalog.py's own pages() trusted every file matching its fixture naming convention under --include-fixtures, with no liveness check, so any bare invocation of the script or the test outside a full preflight.py run inherits a stale leftover from any earlier killed run, by any cause. Added the same os.kill(pid, 0) liveness check gate_no_stray_probe_files already uses, directly in audit_catalog.py's pages(), so a dead-pid fixture is ignored regardless of how the script is invoked. Fail-then-pass proved against the real file: planted a stray fixture with a confirmed-dead pid stating the same wrong price, watched pre-fix code report it as drift, confirmed post-fix code reports 0 findings. test_audit_catalog.py standalone now passes clean (ok, exit 0); py_compile clean. check_urls.py (236/236), affiliate.py --check (165 documents), check_sellable.py (124/126, 2 person-delivered services by design) all re-verified clean after. Removed both stray leftover fixtures this cycle's own mistakes had left behind (confirmed dead pid and untracked via git status before deleting either).

**Went well.** Ran the slow, often-deferred full test suite instead of stopping at --skip-tests, and it earned its keep immediately: it caught a real (if self-inflicted) defect class that a fast pass could never see. Verified the live catalogue directly before writing anything, so a transient test artifact was never mistaken for an actual pricing defect.

## 2026-11-13, scheduled operator cycle: found why no preflight run finishes here, and it was not the hang three entries said it was

**Did.** Attached clean (145 commits). 31 open GitHub issues unchanged since 2026-11-08, none from Phil. No mail credential, unchecked. Production unreachable from this sandbox.

Two things shipped. First, a scorer misattribution: "next to stove storage" scored against Kids Bedroom's Toy Storage Zone on the filler word "next" (an incidental "until the next tidy-up" heading), while Kitchen's Cooking Zone (which discusses "the stove area") lost the tie. "next" joined FORMAT_WORDS; full two-corpus diff clean, 0 status changes, exactly 1 best_page change.

Second, and the one that matters: A125 had handed forward "the test_contact_form_interactive.py hang needs a per-test timeout in gate_tests." Checked first: the timeout already existed and was never the defect, so three cycles handed forward a fix already shipped. Real cause, measured by running it: this sandbox's Chromium starts, forks, then produces zero bytes of `--dump-dom` and never exits on a trivial page. `ops/browser.py`'s `find_browser()` answered from `os.path.exists` alone and called that browser usable, so 20+ browser-driven test files each committed to a 600s render that could not succeed. Fixed: `find_browser()` now proves the browser with one bounded 30s probe and returns None when it cannot render; callers already print "NOT VERIFIED" on None, so no test file needed editing.

**Verified.** `test_contact_form_interactive.py`: 600s-killed to 30s. Five other browser-driven tests now return in under a second, honestly NOT VERIFIED. New `gate_browser_probe_honest` fired with its measured reason. Fail-then-pass proved twice against real code (the pure function, and `find_browser()` itself). `test_keyword_demand.py` 71/71, `test_room_guide_candidates.py` 146/146, `check_urls.py` 236/236, `fix_dashes.py --check` 0/0, `affiliate.py --check` 165 docs, `check_sellable.py` 124/126, `link_graph_report.py` 0 orphans all clean. Live rescore matched the predicted 0 regressions exactly.

**Went well:** checking the handoff instead of executing it turned a fourth no-op cycle into the real root cause.

**Did not go well:** three cycles reported this correctly and acted on it wrongly (CLAUDE.md 0.2: a wrong cause, confidently repeated, costs as much as no report).

**Proven after this entry was first drafted.** The full preflight run this cycle reached its actual end: all 482 test files, start to finish, ~24 minutes, the first complete run in weeks.

**Finishing it immediately earned its keep.** The complete run surfaced `test_cron_delivery_cadence.py` failing, then passing clean minutes later with nothing changed, the tell of an undeterministic test. Root cause: the case stubbed `delivery_gaps` but not the two other live GitHub Actions inputs its check also reads (`gaps_minutes`, `has_push_trigger`), so it claimed to test one seam while depending on two unstubbed live conditions, the same "checks something other than what it says" shape as the browser defect above. Fixed by stubbing all three; proved both directions (simulated punctual-GitHub day: pre-fix case failed as in the real run, fixed case passed; broke the real threshold function: case still goes red naming the real seam). 9/9, checker itself untouched.

**Changing next cycle:** before building on a handed-forward fix, run the one command that confirms the defect is still present. A test stubbing one seam should name which live inputs it still depends on.

**Next:** one thing noticed but not asserted as a defect: fresh `ops/state.json` carries `deploy.reachable: true` alongside empty probes in a sandbox where production is provably unreachable (curl confirmed proxy 403/000 this cycle). May be `resolve_deploy_reachable()` working as designed (never overwrite a measured true with an unmeasured false), or may be the same exists-is-not-works shape just fixed one layer down; worth someone's half hour, not claimed either way. Standing Phil-gated queue otherwise unchanged.

Pushed to main: the scorer fix, the browser probe fix, the new gate and test, the cron test fix, backlog row A126, dashboard regen, this entry. No price or page touched; IndexNow not applicable.
